mechanisms.name: owner-scoped-pty-terminal-registry
mechanisms.what: `TerminalSessionService` is the `ctx.terminals` Cordis `Service` (registered with `super(ctx, 'terminals')`), and its constructor installs `ctx.effect(() => () => this.disposeAll(), 'pty teardown')`. It owns backend registration (`registerBackend`), owner-scoped session maps (`sessions`, `reservedNames`, `pendingSpawns`, `ownerCleanups`, `disposedOwners`), registry-minted ids (`pty-${++this.nextId}`), publication, authorization and awaited cleanup. Every operation funnels through `expectOwned(owner, id)`, which distinguishes `NO_SESSION` from `FOREIGN_SESSION`; `isLiveOwner` requires `ctx.get('agents')?.get(owner.id) === owner` and that the agent is not in `disposedOwners`. Owner teardown is installed with `owner.ctx.effect(...)` on first spawn.
invariants: Backends own terminal mechanics while this service owns ids, publication, authorization, and awaited cleanup. (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts:2-3)
true across the entire spawn-to-close interval, with no publication gap. (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts:229)

Teardown is best-effort: a close failure still clears registries and runs owner cleanups before the aggregated error propagates, so one stuck session cannot orphan backends, reservations, or owner detachers. (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts:437-439)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — eight machine-routable `TerminalErrorCode`s (DUPLICATE_BACKEND, DUPLICATE_NAME, FOREIGN_SESSION, NO_BACKEND, NO_SESSION, OWNER_NOT_LIVE, SEND_ACTIVE, SERVICE_DISPOSING) are thrown via `TerminalError`; disposal aggregates per-session failures into `AggregateError` after clearing registries.

constants.meaning: session id minting scheme (`pty-${++this.nextId}`)
the complete TerminalErrorCode union

mechanisms.name: pty-session-spawn-publication-and-rollback
mechanisms.what: `spawn(owner, request, signal)` validates the service is active, resolves the backend, validates a non-empty name, reserves the owner-local name and a spawn reservation (an `AbortController` plus a settlement promise), mints the session id, and calls `backend.spawn({sessionId, owner, type, name?, cwd?, signal: AbortSignal.any([signal, reservation.signal])})`. Only after setup returns does it re-check the caller signal, `this.disposing` and `isLiveOwner(owner)` before inserting the `SessionRecord` and returning `snapshot(record, session.motd)`. On any failure it rolls the session back with `session.close('PTY spawn rolled back')`, prefers a cancellation failure over the setup error, and throws `AggregateError('PTY spawn and rollback both failed')` when the rollback also failed and the caller signal was not aborted. `TerminalBackendCleanupError` (an `AggregateError` of spawn + cleanup failure) has its `cleanupError` recorded so `abortPendingSpawns` can re-report it during disposal.
invariants: Create an unpublished session or reject after cleaning partial resources; cleanup failure uses TerminalBackendCleanupError. (packages/terminal/terminal/src/types.ts:169)
Create and publish one owner-scoped session after backend setup succeeds. (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts:148)
a cancellation failure is preferred over the setup error when the caller's signal aborted (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts:209-215)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — nothing is published until every post-setup liveness check passes; a failed rollback raises `AggregateError`, and `abortPendingSpawns` collects `cleanupFailure`s into `AggregateError('failed to roll back unpublished PTY setup')`.

constants.meaning: close reason used during spawn rollback

constants.value: 'failed to roll back unpublished PTY setup'
constants.meaning: AggregateError message from abortPendingSpawns

constants.value: 'PTY backend startup and cleanup both failed'
constants.meaning: TerminalBackendCleanupError message

mechanisms.name: pty-send-readiness-state-machine
mechanisms.what: `LocalPtySession.startSend` enforces one active send per session (throwing `TerminalError(..., 'SEND_ACTIVE')`), creates a `LocalSendOperation`, resets readiness evidence, wires the caller abort to `operation.cancel()`, arms an absolute `setTimeout(..., config.timeoutMs)` that settles with `'timeout'`, and starts `beginSend`. `pollReadiness` is the authority: it inspects the foreground process group, and settles on (a) `stdin_read` when `promptSeen && promptTextSeen && idleFor >= pollIntervalMs && foreground.processGroupId === shellPgid`, (b) `stdin_read` when `elapsed >= exactProbeAfterMs` and the foreground group's `inputWaiting` is post-write evidence (`acceptsStdinWait`), or (c) `inferred_idle` when `startupHasOutput && idleFor >= idleSilenceMs + (promptSeen ? handoffGraceMs : 0)`. Session exit and transport failure settle/fail the operation from `onExit`/`onTransportFailure`.
invariants: Keep the exit marker... (n/a here) — the governing rules are: 'Bash can print PROMPT_COMMAND before the kernel publishes its return to the foreground process group. Retain the marker; polling below is the authority that accepts it only after bash owns the foreground.' (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:425-428)

Silence therefore remains the bound on waiting for shell ownership instead of letting a child marker suppress readiness until the absolute timeout. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:505-508)

The same group may still expose the wait that existed before terminal.write. Observe every poll so a departure before the exact-settlement threshold still makes a later return to that wait post-write evidence. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:144-146)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: mixed — a transport failure settles the session as exited (`{kind:'exited', exitCode:null, signal:null}`), fails the active operation, closes the emulator and terminates the terminal; a readiness/inspection failure fails the active send with that error; a timeout settles the send with `'timeout'` rather than throwing.

constants.meaning: default `timeoutMs` — absolute bound for one send and the whole pwsh startup sequence
default `idleSilenceMs` that yields `inferred_idle`
default `exactProbeAfterMs` — delay before exact syscall/foreground probes are trusted
default `pollIntervalMs` readiness polling interval (also the minimum idle before a prompt-based stdin_read)
default `handoffGraceMs` added to idleSilenceMs once a prompt marker was seen
the complete TerminalWaitReason union

mechanisms.name: terminal-ansi-sanitization
mechanisms.what: `TerminalSanitizer` is a streaming control-sequence stripper: `push(chunk)` accumulates into `pending`, walks for `\x1b`, removes OSC sequences (terminated by BEL or ST, and recognizing the owned `PROMPT_MARKER_PREFIX = '133;D;'` inside an OSC payload to set `prompt: true` and start tracking `promptTail`), removes CSI sequences (terminated by any byte in 0x40–0x7e), removes two-byte escapes, and keeps split sequences in `pending` for the next chunk. `enforcePendingBound` drops an over-long incomplete sequence (choosing osc vs csi from `pending[1]`) and `discardPrefix` resumes discarding in the next chunk. `normalizeTerminalText` converts CRLF and lone CR to `\n` and strips BEL; `flush()` emits a trailing printable fragment and restores a trailing CR as a newline.
invariants: Full terminal emulation is deliberately deferred; ordinary line output and the private prompt marker are the supported contract. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/sanitize.ts:21-22)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — a malformed or oversized sequence is dropped rather than raising; `flush()` discards an incomplete trailing escape.

constants.meaning: PROMPT_MARKER_PREFIX inside the OSC payload
CONTROLLED_PROMPT — the exact printable prompt after the marker
final-byte range that terminates a CSI sequence
bound on retained incomplete escape data

mechanisms.name: terminal-bounded-scrollback-and-utf8-truncation
mechanisms.what: `BoundedTextBuffer` retains text under two independent bounds: `maxLines` (splitting on `\n` and keeping only the last `maxLines`, setting `dropped`), then `maxBytes` via `utf8Tail`, which walks the string from the end accumulating whole code points with `Buffer.byteLength` so a UTF-8 character is never split. `consume()` returns the delta plus the `dropped` flag and clears both, so consecutive reads never repeat output; `snapshot()` is non-consuming. `LocalPtySession` uses one `BoundedTextBuffer(config.scrollbackMaxBytes, config.scrollbackLines)` for the scrollback and one `BoundedTextBuffer(maxReadBytes)` per send operation.
invariants: The retained window is measured in UTF-8 bytes and cut on code-point boundaries — `utf8Tail` never splits a character (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:31-43).
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-soft — overflow sets the `truncated`/`dropped` flag and drops the oldest text; nothing throws.

constants.meaning: default `scrollbackLines`
default `scrollbackMaxBytes`
default `maxReadBytes` — per-read and settled-viewport cap; validated to be <= scrollbackMaxBytes at packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/config.ts:116-118
default terminal dimensions and the xterm headless size

mechanisms.name: terminal-emulator-protocol-replies
mechanisms.what: `LocalPtySession` feeds every decoded chunk into an `@xterm/headless` `Terminal` constructed with `{cols, rows, scrollback: 0}`; the emulator's `onData` output (device-status and similar replies a real terminal would send) is written back to the PTY through a serialized `responseWrites` chain. The session tracks `pendingResponseWrites` and an `emulatorWriteDone` latch so `protocolWorkPending()` is true whenever replies or emulator writes are outstanding, and `drainTerminalProtocol()`/`inspectForegroundAfterProtocol()` wait until both chains are quiet before the foreground state is sampled — so a reply generated by the inspected output cannot be mistaken for the shell regaining the foreground.
invariants: Wait until generated replies reach the provider before another send can publish. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:525)
Sample foreground state only after protocol replies are quiet for the entire inspection. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:537)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed on transport — a failed response write calls `onTransportFailure` unless the emulator is closed or the session is closing, which settles the session as exited and terminates the terminal.

constants.meaning: the headless emulator keeps no scrollback of its own (protocol state only)

mechanisms.name: pty-shell-dialect-and-prompt-bootstrap
mechanisms.what: `terminal-bash` is dialect-parameterized. `resolveConfig` picks `shellDialect` (default `'bash'`) and then `shellPath`/`shellArgs`: bash -> `/bin/bash` with `['--noprofile','--norc','-i']`, pwsh -> `resolvePwshPath()` with `['-NoLogo','-NoProfile']`; an explicitly non-empty value always wins (Schemastery materializes an absent array as `[]`, so emptiness means dialect default). `childEnvironment` sets `TERM=dumb, PAGER=cat, GIT_PAGER=cat, DSH_SHELL=1, DSH_SESSION_ID, DSH_PTY_SESSION_ID`; the bash branch adds `PS1='dsh> '`, `PROMPT_COMMAND='printf "\033]133;D;%s\007" "$?"; PS1='dsh> ''` (which re-asserts PS1 each prompt) and `BASH_SILENCE_DEPRECATION_WARNING=1`, while the pwsh branch adds only `NO_COLOR=1` and installs the prompt function `PWSH_PROMPT_SETUP` by writing `ENCODING_PREAMBLE + PWSH_PROMPT_SETUP` as the first startup send. Bash startup goes through `LocalPtySession.initialize`; pwsh startup loops until `waitReason === 'stdin_read'`, accepting only backend stdin-read evidence and bounded by an absolute `timeoutMs`.
invariants: Re-asserting PS1 after the marker keeps prompt readiness working when a command overwrote the shell variable: bash runs PROMPT_COMMAND before rendering each prompt, so an override never survives to the next prompt. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts:83-85)
echoed setup source containing the printable prompt is not readiness (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts:128-130)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — an empty sandbox-produced argv, a `session_exit` or `timeout` wait reason during startup, or a missing `ctx.sandbox` for a confining mode all throw; a startup failure closes the session and rethrows, wrapping a failed cleanup in `TerminalBackendCleanupError`.

constants.meaning: bash dialect defaults
pwsh dialect default arguments
terminal-specific env overrides layered after the subprocess scrub
default `disposeGraceMs`, passed as the terminal spawn's `graceMs`
validated invariant 'so one readiness poll runs inside the grace window'

mechanisms.name: sandbox-mode-fence-for-open-terminals
mechanisms.what: `ensureSandboxModeFence(ctx, owner)` installs one global `owner.ctx.on('internal/dispatch', ...)` listener per agent that reacts only to `'session/event'` events whose `event.type === 'sandbox/mode'` and whose session is the owner's own. It folds the current mode from `sessionProjections.stateOf(session, 'sandboxMode')` or `sandboxPolicy.defaultMode`, and if the requested mode differs while `state.pty.hasOwnerActivity(owner)` is true it throws, refusing the mode change. `spawnArgv` resolves the session's policy and, when the mode is not `danger-full-access`, requires `ctx.get('sandbox')` and replaces the argv with `sandbox.confine(argv, {...policy, mode}).argv`.
invariants: cannot change sandbox mode from "<current>" to "<new>" while persistent terminal sessions are open or being created; wait for creation to settle and close them first (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/index.ts:58-60)
`hasOwnerActivity` is deliberately true across the entire spawn-to-close interval 'with no publication gap' (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts:229)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — the mode-change event throws, and a confining mode without a `ctx.sandbox` provider throws `terminal-bash: sandbox mode "<mode>" requires a ctx.sandbox provider in the execution world`.

constants.meaning: the mode that skips confinement and returns the raw argv
the event type and projection key the fence watches

mechanisms.name: terminal-send-interrupt-on-cancel
mechanisms.what: `LocalSendOperation.cancel()` sets `cancellationRequested`, invokes its `onCancel` callback (which calls `LocalPtySession.interrupt(operation)`) and returns false once already settled. `interrupt` only acts when the operation is still active, marks it as `interrupting`, stops readiness polling and runs `interruptOnce`: it awaits any in-flight provider write (bailing out if it failed), delivers `terminal.signalForeground('SIGINT')`, and then either releases the settled operation or resumes polling immediately (`schedulePoll(operation, 0)`). Cancellation deliberately retains the send slot until the in-flight signal and post-signal polling complete.
invariants: A pre-write inspection failure while cancellation owns the slot must not release it: interruptOnce's in-flight foreground signal could land on a successor's foreground group. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:300-305)
Cancellation owns post-write signalling and reservation release. (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/session.ts:325)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed on the slot, fail-soft on the signal — a signalling failure while the operation is still active escalates to `onTransportFailure`; `cancel()` on a settled operation is a no-op returning false.

constants.meaning: the only signal cancel delivers
immediate poll restart after the interrupt signal

mechanisms.name: terminal-tool-suite
mechanisms.what: `apply(ctx, config)` registers six model-facing tools — `terminal_open`, `terminal_send`, `terminal_read`, `terminal_signal`, `terminal_close`, `terminal_list` — all of which derive the owner from `requireAgent(exec.agent)` and delegate to `ctx.terminals`. It also registers the `tool:pty` system-prompt section. `terminal_open` calls `ctx.terminals.spawn(owner, {type, name?, cwd?}, exec.signal)` and returns the published snapshot plus `motd`; `terminal_send` either starts a `ctx.jobs` job of kind `'pty-send'` (with `outputLimitBytes: maxResultBytes`, `cancel: () => operation.cancel()`, and a `done` mapping that reports `killed` when cancel was requested) or awaits the send with `exec.signal`; `terminal_read` maps offset/count onto `ctx.terminals.read`; `terminal_signal` forwards the signal; `terminal_close` maps `ctx.terminals.kill` to `'closed'`/`'already-closing'`; `terminal_list` returns the owner's snapshots.
invariants: Owner identity comes from the exact tool execution Agent; generic `ctx.jobs` owns background ids and collection. (packages/terminal/tool-terminal/src/index.ts:2-3)

Use a terminal session only when work needs persistent terminal state or interactive stdin ... An inferred_idle or timeout result does not prove the foreground command exited. (packages/terminal/tool-terminal/src/index.ts:159)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed — a missing agent, an empty `sessionId`, a disabled background mode, or a missing `jobs` service throws before any terminal I/O; a foreground send whose `exec.signal` aborted throws `terminal send aborted` after the result is awaited.

constants.meaning: DEFAULT_MAX_RESULT_BYTES cap for one complete model-facing terminal result
MIN_MAX_RESULT_BYTES — smallest cap preserving every counter-backed PTY and job id
the ctx.jobs kind registered by terminal_send
advertised terminal_signal enum; 'Shell-targeted SIGKILL is rejected; use terminal_close'

mechanisms.name: terminal-result-bounding
mechanisms.what: Every terminal tool registers `finalizeContent` which re-bounds the single text block through `boundTerminalText(text, maxResultBytes)`; each `render` also bounds its own output with the same cap. `boundTerminalText` returns the text unchanged when it fits, else appends `TRUNCATED` and retains the HEAD of the text with `TextRetainer({kind:'head'})`. `fitWithPrefix`/`fitWithSuffix`/`boundBodyWithSuffix` keep the metadata suffix (wait reason, session status, line range) or the session prefix visible by budgeting their byte length first and retaining the body's tail.
invariants: Bound one complete terminal acknowledgement while preserving UTF-8 cuts. (packages/terminal/tool-terminal/src/render.ts:88)
Smallest cap that preserves every counter-backed PTY and job id in its creation acknowledgement. (packages/terminal/tool-terminal/src/index.ts:31)
mechanisms.failurePolicy: fail-closed at configuration time — `apply` throws when `maxResultBytes` is not a safe integer or is below `MIN_MAX_RESULT_BYTES`; runtime bounding never throws (it truncates instead).

constants.meaning: TRUNCATED marker appended by every bounded renderer
lower bound enforced both by the schema (.min at :45) and by apply (:149-151)

constants.value: kind: 'head' for the top-level cap, 'tail' for metadata-budgeted bodies
constants.meaning: the TextRetainer direction chosen per renderer

terminal/terminal.note: Real logic, not mere registration: `TerminalSessionService` implements the whole owner-scoped registry — id minting, name/spawn reservations, publication ordering, eight coded failure modes, awaited per-session close, owner-effect cleanup and aggregate disposal (packages/terminal/terminal/src/index.ts:105-474). `types.ts` carries the backend/session/send vocabulary plus `TerminalBackendCleanupError` (packages/terminal/terminal/src/types.ts:18-177). Mechanisms: owner-scoped-pty-terminal-registry, pty-session-spawn-publication-and-rollback.

terminal/terminal-bash.note: Real logic. It IS the local PTY backend: config/dialect resolution plus validation (config.ts), streaming ANSI sanitizer (sanitize.ts), and the 708-line `LocalPtySession` implementing readiness polling, bounded scrollback, the xterm headless protocol-reply loop, interrupt/cancel and idempotent close (session.ts). `index.ts` adds the sandbox-mode fence and the bash/pwsh prompt bootstrap. Mechanisms: pty-shell-dialect-and-prompt-bootstrap, sandbox-mode-fence-for-open-terminals, terminal-ansi-sanitization, terminal-bounded-scrollback-and-utf8-truncation, terminal-emulator-protocol-replies, pty-send-readiness-state-machine, terminal-send-interrupt-on-cancel.

terminal/tool-terminal.note: Real logic beyond registration: six tool definitions with output schemas, background job wiring of kind 'pty-send', presentation hooks, and the `finalizeContent` result-bounding pipeline in render.ts. The `apply` function is the registration entry point but is not a hollow one (validation, config defaulting, prompt section, six tools) (packages/terminal/tool-terminal/src/index.ts:146-401). Mechanisms: terminal-tool-suite, terminal-result-bounding.

notes: All 8 .ts files read in full. Cross-package facts worth carrying: (1) `terminal-bash` depends directly on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-pwsh-local` for `resolvePwshPath` and `ENCODING_PREAMBLE` (packages/terminal/terminal-bash/src/config.ts:4 and src/index.ts:16) — a packages/terminal -> packages/shell dependency. (2) `terminal-bash` reaches the PTY through `ctx.subprocess.spawnTerminal`, so all the subprocess-local containment/identity machinery applies underneath. (3) `isStdinWaiting` from the subprocess inspector is the exact-probe evidence the readiness machine consumes via `SubprocessTerminalForeground.inputWaiting` (session.ts:500); on macOS and Windows that probe always returns false (packages/subprocess/subprocess-local/src/process-inspector.ts:506 and windows-inspector.ts:96), so only the prompt-marker and idle-silence paths can settle there. (4) `tool-bash-persistent`/`tool-pwsh-persistent` consume this service only through `ctx.terminals.spawn/startSend/read/kill/list`. (5) The `idleSilenceMs` default (3_000) is the only 'idle timeout' in this group; the absolute per-send bound is `timeoutMs` (30_000).
